0.0.n: 時間 counts hours of duration here.

0.1.n: After a quantity, 以上 includes that amount and anything greater.

0.2.n: Japanese nouns do not change form to show plural.

0.3.n: と joins dogs and owners as a pair.

0.4.n: 飼い主 specifically refers to someone who keeps an animal.

0.5.n: を is unusual with 会わない here; が would normally mark those not meeting.

0.6.n: 会わない is the plain negative form of 会う.

0.7.n: よう follows the negative verb to describe the situation being arranged.

0.8.n: に links よう to した, forming a phrase about ensuring a situation.

0.9.n: した is the past form of する; ようにした means someone took steps to ensure something.

0.10.n: After a past-form verb, 後 places the next action later.

0.12.n: These are the same animals mentioned before the separation.

0.13.n: と joins the two groups being brought together.

0.14.n: This refers to the animals’ human caretakers.

0.15.n: を marks the dogs and owners as those being made to meet.

0.16.n: 会わせる is the form of 会う meaning to make or let others meet.

0.17.n: という connects the preceding description to 方法, explaining what the method involves.

0.18.n: The preceding clause describes the procedure this noun refers to.

0.19.n: です politely ends the explanation; Japanese uses present tense here.

1.0.n: At the start, 結果 introduces the findings of the procedure.

1.2.n: いつも describes the usual situation of dogs and owners being together.

1.3.n: 一緒 combines with に to describe sharing the same place or activity.

1.4.n: に makes 一緒 describe how the dogs and owners are spending time.

1.5.n: いる describes the presence of living beings, here with 一緒に.

1.6.n: 時 turns the preceding description into a time or situation.

1.7.n: と marks the situation used as the comparison baseline.

1.8.n: 比べて is the linking て-form of 比べる, connecting this comparison to the next line.

2.0.n: 時間 expresses a duration rather than a clock time.

2.1.n: 以上 sets an inclusive lower limit, so exactly five hours also counts.

2.2.n: The noun refers to the animals involved in the procedure.

2.3.n: と links dogs with their owners.

2.4.n: 飼い主 identifies the people who keep and care for the dogs.

2.5.n: This repeats the unusual を before 会わない; standard wording would normally use が.

2.6.n: The negative ending ない shows that contact is being prevented.

2.7.n: よう introduces the intended state of the dogs and owners not meeting.

2.8.n: に connects よう with した to express arranging the stated situation.

2.9.n: The past form した shows the separation procedure happened before the observation.

2.10.n: 後 refers to the period following the arranged separation.

2.11.n: だ links the noun 後 to the conditional と.

2.12.n: と after だ presents the post-separation situation as the condition for the reported change.

2.14.n: 涙 refers to the tears produced by the dogs.

2.15.n: が marks 涙 as what increased.

2.16.n: 多く is the form of 多い used before なる to describe a change in amount.

2.17.n: なった is the past form of なる, indicating a completed change.

2.18.n: そう after a complete statement reports information from another source, rather than describing an appearance.

2.19.n: です makes the report with そう polite.

0.lit: It is a method of making dogs and owners meet after ensuring they do not meet for five-plus hours.
0.tip: ようにした means someone took steps to ensure a situation; 会わせる means to make or let others meet.

1.lit: As a result, compared with when they are always together,
1.tip: と比べて marks a comparison, with the baseline placed before と.

2.lit: When it was after ensuring dogs and owners did not meet for five-plus hours, tears reportedly became more plentiful.
2.tip: A complete statement followed by そうです reports what someone else said or found.
